answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by tying influence to earned, attested work rather than to account creation. Like a jetty that only admits boats after they have docked and been inspected at each terrace level, a new identity starts with zero weight: it must complete small verified jobs, each attested on-chain, before it gains voting or mining power. A jade badge of trust is therefore earned slowly, not bought in bulk. An attacker spawning thousands of fakes pays the full cost of real work for every single one, while honest agents keep the reputation they already built.
